sites.description: The Slide Creek dispersed site has a toilet, fishing access and a sandy beach along the Selway River. Swimming, fishing, floating, canoeing, and kayaking in the river are all popular pasttimes here.

sites.name: Boyd Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Situated along the stunning Selway River, the Boyd Creek Campground contains five camp/RV sites, picnic areas and a restroom. Hikers will enjoy taking a trek up the East Boyd Glover Roundtop National Recreation Trail via one of two trailheads accessing it in the vicinity. Anglers will enjoy fishing in the Selway. The…

sites.name: Glover Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Glover Campground has picnic areas, toilets, a stock ramp and access to two trails: Roundtop Trail #705 and Glover Trail #704. This site is off the main road.

sites.name: Selway Falls Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: The Selway Falls Campground has 7 campsites along Meadow Creek. Boat put-in below the Selway Falls to float to Lowell. The Wild and Scenic section of the Selway River contains Class IV rapids and runs from Paradise Campground to Selway Falls. The Campground will accomodate RV's less than 30-ft. length.

sites.name: Slims Camp
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Slims Camp has picnic areas, toilet and three RV/Trailer pads. Access is very difficult for persons with disabilities. This site is off the main road, has fishing access and access to Meadow Creek National Recreation Trail. Stock facilities available for equestrians.

sites.name: Race Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Three camp sites on the Upper Selway River. Boat put-in below Selway Falls. A trailhead at the campground goes east along the Selway River, providing access to the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness. Stock facilities are available for equestrians. The wild and scenic section of the Selway contains Class IV rapids and runs…

sites.name: Bridge Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Nestled in tall timber, with a creek running through, Bridge Creek Campground has campsites with tables and metal fire rings.

sites.name: Castle Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Castle Creek Campground is located along the South Fork of the Clearwater River at milepost 14 on Highway 14 east of Grangeville, Idaho. The campground has 9 units with picnic tables, water, and toilets. There is also access for RVs and trailers. This is a first-come first-served campground. The water system is…

sites.name: Crooked River Campground #3
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: One camp pad with a toilet. Well-screened by tall, dense timber. Across the road from Crooked River.

sites.name: Ditch Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Ditch Creek Campground sports campsites in an open area with few tall trees - a beautiful place to "catch the sun."

sites.name: Dixie Meadow Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Dispersed campsite with toilet.

sites.name: Five Mile Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Situated in open, tall timber, this campground is popular for family camping, in that it is near a fishing and swimming pond (Five Mile Pond), has a creek flowing by the site, and has easy access to Crooked River. Fire rings with camp sites grace the campground.

sites.name: French Gulch Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: French Gulch Campground provides a good "base camp" for day trips to other areas of the Red River Ranger District, with two campsites and vault toilet. This is a roomy area, with plenty of parking available. It provides public fishing access on nearby Red River. French Gulch Creek flows through the campground.

sites.name: Halfway House Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Halfway House Campground rests in tall timber with a small creek running through. There are campsites with tables and fire rings. Stock facilities (feed bunk and loading ramp) are nearby. This is a popular access site into the Gospel Hump Wilderness Area via Crooked Creek Trail #215.

sites.name: Leggett Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Just 14 miles west of Elk City off Highway 14, Leggett Creek campground provides easy access to larger RV's and trailers in its five campsites, serviced by a metal fire ring and one SST (Sweet Smelling Toilet). There are no refuse receptacles provided. It provides public fishing access to Leggett Creek and the South…

sites.name: Limber Luke Campground and Trailhead
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: This trailhead serves Anderson Butte National Recreation Trail (#505). Located in open timber, with a toilet, stock loading ramp, fire ring and parking space for five camper vehicles, it is very popular with big game hunters.

sites.name: Mackay Bar Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Resting near the north bank of the mighty Salmon River, Mackay Bar campground offers three campsites, tables and fire grates. Parking is limited. Access to this campground is via a very rough, winding road with many tight switchbacks. Low-range, 4-wheel drive is recommended, with no trailers. Note : Be considerate of…

sites.name: Mallard Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Mallard Creek Campground provides five campsites situated in the tall timber near Mallard Creek. Although there is a toilet, there are no tables or fire grates.

sites.name: Meadow Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Meadow Creek Campground is located along the South Fork of the Clearwater River. The campground has 3 units with picnic tables and toilets.

sites.name: O'Hara Saddle Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: O'Hara Saddle campground is at the edge of a meadow on an open ridge top. The campground is a nice location to park your OHV and camp for the night It provides fire rings and two camp pads. There is no toilet currently available. Heaviest use is by hunters during big game season.

sites.name: Red River Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Red River Campground has campsites with tables and metal fire rings. Several toilets service the campground. Larger RVs should preview the site before entering.

sites.name: Sam's Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Sam's Creek Campground, near the Gospel-Hump Wilderness on Crooked Creek and Sams Creek, is peacefully tucked in among a grove of pine trees with the soothing sounds of the river running in the background. Three campsites, tables and fire grates allow for relaxed camping. There is limited parking and limited…

sites.name: Sing Lee Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Sing Lee Campground rests near tall timber providing for open shade in the afternoon. A small creek flows through the site, while Newsome Creek is just across the road. The campground provides four camp pads, with two metal fire rings and two tables.

sites.name: South Fork Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: South Fork Campground, located off Highway 14 along the South Fork of the Clearwater River, has 9 sites for RVs and tent campers. You may find a Volunteer Campground Host during the operating season. Site #3 is 31 feet long, and site #8 is 25 feet long. All other sites are shorter.

sites.name: Table Meadows Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Situated in a popular big game hunting area, Table Meadows Campground offers two toilets, two stock feeding bunks, a loading ramp, hitching rail and six camp pads. The West Fork of the American River flows through the campground.

sites.name: Ten Mile
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: This campsite is the trailhead for Ten Mile Creek Trail #415 and sports a loading ramp, hitching rail, toilet and two camping pads. Ten Mile Creek flows through the campsite.

sites.name: Trapper Creek Camp Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: The Trapper Creek camp area provides one camp pad located in tall timber next to South Fork Red River, a toilet and information board. The parking area serves as a snow park in the winter for on/off loading snowmobiles to access groomed snowmobile trails.

sites.name: Wildhorse Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Six campsites on Wildhorse Lake, in a lovely riparian meadow. A trail from the campground leads into the Wilderness, into Tenmile Meadows. Another trailhead is south of the campground and leads deep into the Wilderness, all the way to Sugarloaf Butte.

sites.name: Dry Saddle Trailhead
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Dry Saddle trailhead is one of the major trailheads accessing the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness lying north of the Salmon River. It provides access to many high mountain lakes along Sheep Hill Trail #575. It is only a 10-mile hike to Sheep Hill Lookout. A loading ramp is provided for stock. The 250 degree…

sites.name: Granite Springs Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Granite Springs campground has four campsites with metal fire rings, but no tables. It is an excellent area to stop and spend the night as you’re traveling the Magruder Corridor. OHV riding is popular along the Magruder Corridor and on other Forest Service roads in the area. The campground has an information board and…

sites.name: Poet Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Poet Creek Campground is situated in tall timber. Four stock mangers are located south of the campground.

sites.name: Fish Creek Group Use Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: This is the primitive Fish Creek Dispersed Group Use Site, located 1 mile south of the Fish Creek Campground. It may be reserved for up to 75 people. This site has also been called "Eagle's Nest", "Girl Scout Camp," and "Fish Creek Dispersed Site." There is no electricity, water, or sewer hookups at this group use…

sites.name: Rocky Bluff Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: Located on the cusp of the magical and mysterious Gospel-Hump Wilderness, hikers, campers, anglers, hunters and families alike will find four campsites with parking, picnic tables, firerings and a trailhead marking a trail which skirts the edge of the Wilderness. Campground area does not offer adequate room to…

sites.name: North Fork Slate Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: The North Fork Slate Creek Campground consists of five campsites, picnic tables and firerings located at the confluence of Slate Creek and its North Fork. Hikers as well as mountain bikers can enjoy a number of loop trails in the area. Parking is suitable for up to five vehicles. Small tent/travel trailers can be…

sites.name: Iron Phone Junction Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
sites.description: This area has four campsites with fire rings, hitching rails, and no feed bunks provided.

sites.name: Douglas Fir Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This campground is situated in the forest along the North Fork Nooksack River. Tall Douglas Fir, western red cedar, and western hemlock trees provide abundant shade. Guided river rafting and white water kayaking opportunities are available on the river. A day use picnic shelter provides a space for groups to gather…

sites.name: Silver Fir Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This campground is situated in the forest along the North Fork Nooksack River. Most of the sites are removed from the highway and a short walk to the river. Many Silver fir, western red cedar, and western hemlock trees provide shade, but a very sunny gravel bar is between the campground and the river.

sites.name: Bayview Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: Bayview Campground and Bayview North Group Site (approximately 1/4 mile north from the campground) are located along the Baker Lake Road approximately 14.8 miles from State Route 20. Bayview Campground sits along the shore of Baker Lake in the stunning Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. This campground was…

sites.name: Boulder Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This smaller sized campground is situated in a lovely forested setting along Boulder Creek in the Baker Lake basin. This tranquil setting is in close proximity to the shores of Baker Lake.

sites.name: Horseshoe Cove Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This popular destination campground is situated on the western shore of Baker Lake. Campsites are situated in a forested setting with pathways connecting down to the lakeshore. Day use includes a swimming beach and a gravel boat launch area with parking. The campground includes 38 tent/trailer sites, 2 of which are…

sites.name: Mineral Park Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: Mineral Park is about 15 miles from the town of Marblemount, and about 7.5 miles past Marble Creek Campground along the gravel Cascade River Road. This remote campground is situated near the confluence of the North and South Forks of the Cascade River segment of the Skagit Wild & Scenic River System.. It is in close…

sites.name: Beaver Creek Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: Beaver Creek campground is a popular group camp, situated along the south fork Stillaguamish River with a view of Big Four Mountain. The area is fairly flat making it an excellent site for small children. This campground can accommodate up to 25 people. In addition to fishing, there are opportunities nearby for hiking…

sites.name: Coal Creek Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This campground is situated along the South Fork Stillaguamish River. This campground is a sandy, ideal place for children.

sites.name: Esswine Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: Situated amongst the trees, this campground has sites on both sides of the short road that parallels the Mountain Loop Highway. There is a moderate amount of traffic noise, with the campground lying a short distance from the South Fork Stillaguamish River.

sites.name: Tulalip Mill Site Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: Located in a flat area making it ideal for campers or trailers. A short trail leads to the South Fork Stillaguamish River.

sites.name: Troublesome Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: Troublesome Creek Campground offers 25 sites nestled in a mixed conifer forest on the banks of the scenic North Fork Skykomish River and its tributary, Troublesome Creek. Water is abundant in this area, offering visitors easy access to fishing, kayaking, and swimming. There is also a mile long nature trail that…

sites.name: San Juan Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: A nice combination of sun and shade, this campground offers exploration of the North Fork of the Skykomish river when you're not sitting by the campfire roasting marshmallows.

sites.name: Middle Fork Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This campground is located along the Middle Fork of the Snoqualmie River. The site is forested with Douglas-fir, cedar and western hemlock, providing abundant shade. From the western part of the campground access the CCC Trail. Turn left at first junction and cross Middle Fork Road to the Middle Fork Trailhead and…

sites.name: Dalles Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: This campground is next to the White River in an old growth forest with Douglas-fir, cedar and western hemlock trees, providing abundant shade.

sites.name: Evans Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
sites.description: EMERGENCY CLOSURE: SR-165 MP 11.5 Carbon River Bridge is closed. Access to this site is unavailable at this time. This campground is located in a beautiful forest setting offering 40 miles of combined four-wheel drive and motorcycle/quad trails of varying difficulty. A covered picnic shelter is available on first come…

sites.name: Buttercup Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: A small, quiet campground, this site is primarily used by river paddlers. Located in stands of mixed hardwoods and pine, campers may be surprised by a wildlife visitor or two while enjoying close-up views of the river. Brochure with map : This brochure is set to print on 11 x 17 paper, landscape (wide) orientation. To…

sites.name: Cathedral Pines Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: The access road is gated to prohibit motorized access. Visitors to this campground are primarily river paddlers. To access the site from the road, visitors will need to walk .25 miles into the large, old-growth eastern white pine to find the campground. Trees offer a screen from the river, but still allow campers…

sites.name: Meadow Springs Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Located on the edge of a red pine plantation, visitors to this site may see many varieties of wildlife in addition to their view of the Au Sable River. This camping area is a short .25 mile walk from the gate, but is primarily used by river paddlers. There is no motorized access to this site. Brochure with map : This…

sites.name: River Dune Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Located between the Au Sable River Scenic Overlook and Au Sable Loop Campground, this small site is a short .5 mile walk from the gate. Set back from the road and camping area, campers can enjoy views of the river. Visitors can access the river from a short set of stairs located near the site. Brochure with map : This…

sites.name: Claybanks Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This river access is on the flies only, catch and release portion of the river. The river bottom is mostly gravel and is a very good area for brown trout. The path to the river borders posted private land on one side before reaching the stairs to the river. The stairs to the river are steep, and will be a workout for…

sites.name: Elk Canoe Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This campground is located in the middle of the 66-mile Scenic portion of the river. The camps are set back from the river in openings within a forested setting. As paddlers travel down the river they will see many meadows and locations to fish. Some campers will park at Upper Branch Bridge and walk to the campsites…

sites.name: Sulak Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This site is primarily used by anglers, hunters and families for camping. There is a short, .25 mile walk from the campsites to the river, through federal and state land. The river access is operated by the MI-DNRE. Brochure with Map : This brochure is set to print on 11 x 17 paper, landscape (wide) orientation. To…

sites.name: Diamond Point
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Diamond Point campground is surrounded by white pine forest. The most common use for the site is for canoe launching, particularly on weekends.

sites.name: Bear Track Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Bear Track got its name many years ago from a bear track found while building the site. A 1.5 mile trail connects the campground to the North Country National Scenic Trail. Fishing is a popular activity for this area. Map: This brochure is set to print on 8.5x11 paper, landscape (wide) orientation.

sites.name: Pine River Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This is a popular campground during fishing season. Recreation opportunities include hunting, picnicking, mushroom gathering and berry picking. The picnic shelter is a Civilian Conservation Corps construction from the mid 1940's.

sites.name: Au Sable Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Along the Au Sable River is the Au Sable Special Area, a 10,628 acre area characterized by flat to gently rolling hills with some steep banks along the Au Sable River. This area is located in Iosco and Alcona counties. The Au Sable Special Area stretches the southern end of Alcona Dam Pond (Bamfield Road) to just…

sites.name: Bowman Lake Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This area not only has the Pere Marquette River running through it, but also contains a portion of the North Country National Scenic Trail and habitat for the federally endangered Karner blue butterfly. The Bowman Lake area is located in Lake and Sweetwater Townships in Lake County. A total of 1,145 acres of NFS lands…

sites.name: Condon Lakes West
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This area is very popular for mushroom and berry picking, as well as hunting, fishing and camping.

sites.name: Whelan Lake Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This area is popular for canoeing, fishing and camping. The camping area is near the south branch of the Pere Marquette River, on Whelan Lake. The land surrounding the lake is primarily federal ownership.

sites.name: Wakeley Lake Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: A moderatly sized area to take a hike or view wildlife, this area also offers canoeing opportunities. The lake tapers out into a swampy marsh area along the shoreline in some areas. Visitors to the area will be treated to a forested setting that varies from tag alder and conifer swamps to upland jack and white pine…

sites.name: Horseshoe Lake Campground and Boat Launch
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: The small 16-acre lake offers a variety of fishing opportunities. The one-mile walk around the north end of the lake provides for wildlife sightings and scenic views of the lake and campground. This campground is small and lightly used, perfect for those looking for solitude.

sites.name: Jewell Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Jewell Lake Campground is located on the east side of the 193-acre Jewell Lake. This lake offers a wide variety of fishing and boating opportunities. A snowmobile trail runs through the area during the winter months.

sites.name: Bowman Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: The campground is walk-in only, with carry-in canoe access. This quiet and secluded campground is very popular with fisherman and hunters. Brochure with Map : This brochure is set to print on 11 x 17 paper, landscape (wide) orientation. To print on 8 1/2 x 11 paper set the print area to "shrink to printable area"…

sites.name: Brush Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: The campground is located on the shores of Brush Lake, which is entirely surrounded by National Forest System lands. There is a drive-in boat launch on the eastern shore of the river and a smaller carry-in boat launch in the campground. This site is very popular with anglers and hunters. It is also a popular wildlife…

sites.name: Hemlock Campground and Boat Launch
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This campground is located on the west end of Lake Mitchell near Cadillac. The lake is 1,600 acres and nearly surrounded by residences. The west end of the lake is marshy and good for wildlife viewing. The lake is not good for swimming at this end, due to milfoil and other plants. Flickr Photo Album

sites.name: Highbank Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This campground is located on the 20-acre Highbank Lake, which is completely surrounded by National Forest System land. This is a popular campground for anglers and hikers. The beach is very swim friendly, shallow with a sandy bottom.

sites.name: Indian Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Indian Lake Campground is located on the 34-acre Indian Lake. The lake is surrounded by national forest, except a few small private ownerships on the northwest and southeast sides of the lake. The lake has clear water and a sandy bottom, and is popular for fishing. A boat launch provides both motorized and…

sites.name: Minnie Pond Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This site is located on Minnie Pond on a human-made impoundment. Ducks, geese and heron frequent the area. This is a popular area for small and large game and waterfowl hunting. A foot bridge on Mena Creek connects the campground to the day use area. The day use area is located on the side of the creek. No ORV's are…

sites.name: Old Grade Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Located on the Little Manistee River, this campground is completely surrounded by National Forest System land. There is a short interpretive hiking trail with foot bridges from the campground through a hemlock and birch forest. The campground is loctated near wetlands and many fields, making it an excellent area to…

sites.name: Pine Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Pine Lake Campground is located on the shores of beautiful Pine Lake. The east side of the lake is mostly privately owned and has many cabins. The west side is federally owned and is swampy and has been occupied by bald eagles over the years. The beach off the picnic area is shallow for a long distance out and gravel…

sites.name: Shelley Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Shelley Lake is a 15-acre lake, surrounded by National Forest land, the family-style campground is the only access to the lake. A foot-bridge over the creek leads to one of the sites. This campground is very popular during fishing season. Sites are surrounded by an oak and maple forest. The lake is only 15-feet at its…

sites.name: Timber Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: The campground is located near a small impoundment, however the impoundment is not a popular site for fishing. The busiest use is the North Country National Scenic Trail trailhead located in the campground. In the winter this site is plowed and provides access to the Ward Hills Snowmobile Trail. ORV use is prohibited…

sites.name: Twinwood Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Bigelow Creek feeds into Twinwood Lake next to the campground and creates a good current in the lake. Ice fishing is a very popular on this lake. This beautiful area is forested with white pine and provides ample opportunity for wildlife viewing. Swans frequent the lake, and eagles have historically nested in the…

sites.name: Walkup Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: This campground is located on Walkup Lake.

sites.name: Benton Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Benton Lake is a 33-acre lake completely surrounded by National Forest land. The North Country National Scenic Trail is located off Pierce Drive, about 2 miles east of the campground entrance road. This site is usually quiet, but there are lots of activities, including fishing, swimming, picnicking and hiking. This…

sites.name: Lake Michigan Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Lake Michigan Recreation Area is a four loop campground located on the shoreline to Lake Michigan between Manistee and Ludington. In addition to the 99 single family sites and 3 group sites, the site also boasts a day use area with multiple picnic tables, pavilions and a playground, an ampitheater and an overlook…

sites.name: Sand Lake Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Sand Lake Recreation Area is the only public access on this lake. The ownership around the lake is primarily private. The beach is sandy and clean, but further out the lake bottom becomes mucky. The lake is mostly shallow, with a few deeper areas. The campsites are open within the wooded area. Flickr Photo Album

sites.name: Rollways Campground and Day Use Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Huron-Manistee National Forests
sites.description: Rollways Campground was built in 1909 and was one of the first campgrounds established on the Huron. The pull-through campsites accommodate large motor homes and trailers. sites.name: Valle Tio Vinces Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Gila National Forest
sites.description: Valle Tio Vinces Campground is a partially developed campground on the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail. Although there is no water available it is still a nice resting spot for hikers and bike riders. There are also horse corrals for equestrians looking for a place to camp.

sites.name: Armijo Springs Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Gila National Forest
sites.description: A real jewel of a secluded partially developed campground in ponderosa pine. Armijo Springs Campground is a secluded quiet campground off the beaten path, yet it is not too far from Quemado Lake. sites.description: The Riverview Campground sits at an elevation of just under 8000 feet. Fishing in the Yellowstone River for rainbow, cutthroat, and brown trout is popular. There is trailhead access to the High Uintas Wilderness at the end of Forest Road #124 at the Swift Creek Trailhead.

sites.name: Reservoir Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: The Reservoir Campground sits at an elevation of 7900 feet near the Yellowstone Reservoir and the Yellowstone River. Trailhead access to the High Uintas Wilderness is at the end of Forest Road #124 at the Swift Creek Trailhead.

sites.name: Bridge Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: The Bridge Campground is at over 7600 feet adjacent to the Yellowstone River.

sites.name: Kingfisher Island Boat-in Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: This campground has 8 boat-in only tent camping sites on the east shore of Kingfisher Island, a large island in the southwest arm of Flaming Gorge Reservoir. sites.name: Deep Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: This campground is at the northern edge of the Uinta Mountains. There is no water or garbage service . Nearby Activities: Elk Park Trail leads south into the mountains. There is a shorter trail that goes northwest to Summit Springs. Fishing for rainbow trout in Deep Creek is popular in this area.

sites.name: Carmel Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: This developed campground has interpretive displays which help you appreciate the magic of the surrounding area. Nearby Activities: Sheep Canyon Geological Area, just west of the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area, features stunning scenic panoramas, framed by colorfully-striated cliffs.

sites.name: Spirit Lake Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: The campground is tucked into a mix of conifers and is located beside Spirit Lake. No water or garbage service is available.

sites.name: Stonefly I River Camp
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: Stonefly I River Camp is on the north side of river 8.2 miles below dam and 1.0 miles below Little Hole. Sites are along…

sites.name: Sand River Camp
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: Sand is on the north side of the river 8.3 miles below dam and 1.1 miles below Little Hole. Site has one table, one fire ring, three tent pads (fits up to four or five tents), portable toilet screen and two benches. Site has natural shade. Capacity: 8-10 people. Campers can hike in from Little Hole or boat in from the…

sites.name: Sheep Creek Bay Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: This campground is convenient to boat ramp with four sites on asphalt.
sites.openingHours: May - Opening date may be adjusted due to weather – September

sites.name: Uinta River Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: Uinta River Group campground is located in ponderosa pine trees, near the Uinta River. The site is not paved.

sites.name: Dutch John Draw Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Ashley National Forest
sites.description: Dutch John Draw Campground is located within a quiet cove on Flaming Gorge Reservoir. It is located on a sloping hillside forested with pinyon pines, which offer little shade. The entire site offers scenic views of the water. Campers enjoy easy access to boating, water skiing, fishing and swimming. A small boat dock…

sites.name: Devils Canyon Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Devils Canyon Campground is located just 13 miles south of Monticello, Utah at an elevation of 7,400 feet. Ponderosa pines, pinyon pines, and junipers cover the area offering limited shade. Summer temperatures are warm in the day and cool in the evening. Popular attractions in the area include Canyonlands, Arches, and…

sites.name: Foy Lake Fishing/Camping Site
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: The Foy Lake Fishing and Camping Site is located next to Foy Lake, a 4.2 acre lake located about 1.0 miles off FH 49 Loop/Harts Draw down Spring Lake Road #100. The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Rainbow Trout.

sites.name: Buckeye Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Buckeye Recreation Area sits at an elevation of 7600 ft on the east side of the La Sal Mountains surrounded by ponderosa pine trees. sites.name: Bridges Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: This is located in beautiful Huntington Canyon, along the Huntington Canyon National Scenic Byway on Utah Highway 31. It is situated at an elevation of approximately 8,700 feet. Many recreational activities are available, including hiking, biking, scenic driving, and fishing. This is a "pack it in, pack it out" site…

sites.name: Chute Group Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Chute Group Campground is located in beautiful Huntington Canyon, along the Huntington Canyon National Scenic Byway on Utah Highway 31. sites.name: Mason Draw Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Mason Draw Campground offers 5 first come/first serve campsites that are available for $10/night. It is located just off the La Sal Loop Road near the Castle Valley Overlook. sites.name: Oowah Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Oowah Lake Campground sits at 8800 ft. elevation in the spectacular La Sal mountains. There are 11 tent-only, first come/ first serve campsites next to the small but scenic Oowah Lake. Trailhead access from the campground includes the Clarks Lake, Boren Mesa, Moonlight Meadows, and Warner Lake trails. Hike a short…

sites.name: Dalton Springs Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: There are sixteen first come/ first serve campsites in an aspen and gambel oak grove at 8200 ft elevation. There are multiple trails and roads nearby offering recreation opportunities for biking, hiking, motorized activities, and equestrian use. Mule deer, black bears, and other wildlife may be seen nearby. Newspaper…

sites.name: Lake Canyon Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Lake Canyon Recreation Area is located along Utah's scenic Energy Loop on top of the Wasatch Plateau off Hwy 31 approximately 18 miles east of Fairview, Utah. Situated between Huntington and Cleveland Reservoirs at an approximate elevation of 9,000 feet, this area is a fishing and ATV paradise. Vault toilets are…

sites.name: Potters Pond Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Potters Pond Campground is located in a high mountain valley in Upper Joes Valley. It is next to two sparkling ponds at an elevation of 9,000 feet. Grasses and pine trees cover the area, and aspen trees dot the surrounding mountainsides. This campground offers a variety of campsites, including single, double and…

sites.name: River Bend Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: River Bend Campground is a primitive campsite nestled in a shaded area alongside Huntington Creek. This campground is located in beautiful Huntington Canyon along the Huntington Canyon National Scenic Byway on Utah Highway 31. It sits at an elevation of approximately 7,100 feet. Many recreational activities are…

sites.name: Upper Joes Valley Dispersed Site
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Upper Joes Valley is located at ~7340' elevation, just south of the intersection of Millers Flat Road and Lowry Water Road. The trees offer shade for most campers and provide spectacular autumn color. Many people enjoy the solitude and primitive experience of camping away from developed campgrounds and other campers…

sites.name: Upper Six Mile Ponds Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Upper Six Mile Ponds Campground is just ten miles from Sterling, Utah at an elevation of 8,400 feet. A mixed forest of spruce, pinyon, juniper, fir, and aspen covers the area, offering partial shade. Summer wildflowers and wildlife are abundant. Canoeing and fishing for trout are popular at the ponds. Many people…

sites.name: Chicken Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Manti-La Sal National Forest
sites.description: Elevation 6200 feet. 8 shady sites, set among pines in Chicken Creek Canyon. Fishing is good in Chicken Creek. Pets must be leashed in campground.

sites.name: Beartree Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Due to Hurrican Helene impacts, Bever Flats, Chipmunk Circle, and group camping are closed for the 2025 season. Picnicking and day use are available beginning 5/16.

sites.name: Blowing Springs Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Offering both sunny and shaded camping sites, visitors to Blowing Springs Campground will be amazed by the phenomenon for which this site is named. sites.name: Camp Run Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Nestled along a Shenandoah Mountain drainage in Pendleton County, WV, Camp Run provides an opportunity for primitive 1950’s style camping that is popular with hunters.

sites.name: Cane Patch Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Cane Patch Campground is within walking distance of Phillips Creek Day Use Area. The campground has 35 campsites, 7 of which have electric hookups.

sites.name: Greenwood Point Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Greenwood Point Campground at Lake Moomaw offers the solitude of an isolated and remote location. With no road access, the adventure is just getting there! sites.name: Hawk Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Hawk Campground sits nestled in the Alleghany Mountains surround by a spectacular nature setting. Experience an exciting hiking experience with easy access to the Tuscarora Trail right from the campground. In the fall, this inviting location offers hunters a secluded environment to stay overnight. Fall asleep to the…

sites.name: Hidden Valley Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: With vast fields of wildflowers that attract countless butterflies, birds, and other wildlife, the Hidden Valley Recreation Area is appropriately named due to its secluded and hidden feeling. Drawing visitors for hundreds of years, the valley is a historic location with an antebellum-era mansion which is now run as a…

sites.name: High Knob Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: The High Knob Recreation Area was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in the late 1930’s. This remote and private location offers cooler summer temperatures due to its higher mountain elevation. The area offers a campground and day use and picnic area along a scenic mountain lake. Many of the original CCC…

sites.name: Hone Quarry Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Hone Quarry Campground is within one mile of Hone Quarry Reservoir. Nearby trailheads lead to popular rock climbing areas. Highlights of the campground include a picturesque stream, a hike to a nearby 15-foot waterfall and an adjacent group picnic shelter that is non-fee and is available first-come first-served.

sites.name: Little Fort Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Little Fort is a first-come-first-serve minimally developed recreation area located near the meadow that was once a rest stop for a stagecoach line. Enjoy the thrill of riding the largest OHV system in the state of Virginia with easy access right from the campground to the Peters Mill Run/Taskers Gap OHV trail system.

sites.name: McClintic Point Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: McClintic Point at Lake Moomaw sits on the northern end of the lake. Enjoy the easygoing, peaceful vibe of McClintic Point's rustic campground set among scattered trees and open fields. This angler's paradise provides plentiful shoreline fishing and some lakefront campsites. Boating, canoeing, water skiing and and…

sites.name: North Creek Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Located along the edge of North Creek, this campground offers shady campsites and a relaxed atmosphere. Prop your feet up and listen to the stream as it gurgles past, or take advantage of the fishing at your door.

sites.name: North River Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: This open area campground was originally constructed as a CCC camp. Evidence of the original sites and logging trails still remain today. North River Gorge is a popular hiking, biking, and fishing area with a swinging bridge spanning the North River. Close proximity to Wild Oak National Recreation Trail, Stanton Dam…

sites.name: Old Virginia Group Horse Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: This campground is a primitive horse camp with room for 6 to 15 horse trailers depending on the sizes. It offers easy access to the Virginia Highlands Horse Trail with its connections to the Iron Mountain Trail. From the Iron Mountain Trail, riders can also access the New River Trail.

sites.name: Shaws Fork Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: This campground provides access to trailheads and is popular among hunters. This site is also near the historic Civil War battlefield in McDowell, VA.

sites.name: Steel Bridge Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Enjoy splashing or fishing in the cool water of Potts Creek, a stocked trout stream adjacent to this rustic campground and day use area. sites.name: Stony Fork Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Stony Fork is located in a natural forest setting at the foot of Big Walker Mountain and adjacent to the Big Walker Scenic Byway. A short drive from I-77 and I-81, the campground is popular with RVers and tent campers. The East Fork of Stony Fork Creek winds through the campground and provides water play and trout…

sites.name: The Pines Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: The Pines is a rustic campground in a wooded setting, located adjacent to Barbour's Creek, a stocked trout stream. sites.name: Todd Lake Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Visitors to Todd Lake Recreation Area enjoy a historic campground complete with a wheelchair accessible beach. A children’s playground, plenty of open fields, grills, and picnic tables make this location an ideal place to spend a relaxing summer afternoon. Explore multiple trails from this location popular among…

sites.name: Walnut Flats Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: This small, primitive campground is well suited for tent camping but also accommodates small recreation vehicles. It has shaded sites clustered around a grassy opening surrounded by forest. sites.name: White Cedar Horse Camp
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Built in 2006, this campground is located on top of Flat Top Mountain. It is perfect for camping with horses; there is plenty of shade and every site has a metal pipe corral. sites.name: White Rocks Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: White Rocks Campground is in a secluded forest setting with cool summertime temperatures and great wildlife watching opportunities. sites.name: Wolf Gap Recreation Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · George Washington & Jefferson National Forest
sites.description: Wolf Gap Recreation Area was once the site of a 1930’s African American Civilian Conservation Corps Camp. This recreation area has many hiking opportunities nearby. sites.name: Thomas Hunting Grounds Yellow Post Sites
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · San Bernardino National Forest
sites.description: These five remote camping sites offer locations for tent and car camping. There are some mature shade trees near the sites, but other than a metal fire ring for campfires, these sites do NOT contain the amenities found at developed campgrounds. There is no water, no picnic tables, no restrooms nearby, and no trash…

sites.name: Clark's Ranch Yellow Post Site
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · San Bernardino National Forest
sites.description: This single remote camp site offers an isolated scenic location ideal for tent and car camping or a relaxing picnic far from the crowds. sites.name: Santa Rosa Yellow Post Sites
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · San Bernardino National Forest
sites.description: Santa Rosa Mountain has 14 remote camping sites scattered across the high ridges offering isolated scenic campsites ideal for tent and car camping or a relaxing picnic far from the crowds. sites.name: Thomas Mountain & Toolbox Springs Yellow Post Site
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · San Bernardino National Forest
sites.description: There are 10 Yellow Post sites in the Thomas Mountain area, and Toolbox Spring area has 6 remote camping sites. They offer isolated scenic locations ideal for tent and car camping or a relaxing picnic. Other than a metal pit for campfires, these sites do NOT contain the amenities found at developed campgrounds. There…

sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · San Bernardino National Forest
sites.description: This 2 mile road travels from the junction of Coxey OHV Road 3N14 to the forest boundary in the north. Important Note: Non-street legal vehicles cannot travel south of the junction of 4N16 and 3N14. All non-street legal vehicles must turn right (north) on 3N14.

sites.name: Chirpchatter Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Shasta-Trinity National Forest
sites.description: Located east of Shasta Lake, these remote campsites offer the perfect spot to relax. Forested and shady, this is a perfect home base for your OHV adventures! sites.name: Crocker Pond Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: This secluded, 7 site campground is located on the edge of Crocker Pond under a towering white pine forest. Crocker Pond along with several other nearby fishing ponds have boat launches for non-motorized boats.

sites.name: Gentian Pond Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: This 3 sided shelter (and tent platforms) are located at Gentian Pond,along the Appalachian Trail in the Mahoosuc Range.

sites.name: Hermit Lake Shelters
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: At the base of Tuckerman Ravine, this shelter provides access to year-round mountaineering opportunities on the East side of Mt. sites.name: Imp Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: The Imp shelter (and tent platforms) provide backcountry camping opportunities in the heart of the Carter-Moriah range, located on a spur trail off the Appalachian Trail. Caretaker on site in summer.

sites.name: Mt Cabot Cabin
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest

sites.name: Osgood Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Popular tent site on the Appalachian Trail, near the Great Gulf Wilderness on the South side of Mt. Madison. Five tent platforms available (capacity: 20). Reliable water nearby and outhouse on site.

sites.name: Rattle River Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Rattle River Shelter is reached by hiking 1.7 miles up the gradual grade of the Rattle River Trail. In addition to the shelter, 3 designated tent sites provide for overflow camping.

sites.name: Trident Col Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Found off of the Mahoosuc Trail (AT) this site provides 4 tentsites and a composting toilet.

sites.name: Unknown Pond Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Nestled next to calm waters of Unknown Pond, this tent site is located off a spur of the Unknown Pond Trail. There is an outhouse, 6 designated camping spaces and reliable water from the pond or stream.

sites.name: Valley Way Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Located on a spur path off the Valley Way Trail, 3.1 miles from the Appalachia parking area, this site offers 5 mineral pad tent sites. On the North side of Mt. Madison, there is the opportunity to enjoy several scenic waterfalls on the way to this site.

sites.name: Beaver Brook Shelter

sites.name: Big Rock Campground
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​This campground is named after one of the many large boulders dropped from the glaciers that shaped this region. sites.name: Campton Day Use Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Formerly a campground, this site has been re-opened as a day use area. It is a wonderful setting for a family picnic with newly installed fire grates for grilling, picnic tables, a large grassy area for any number of activities, and a newly installed trail to a restroom.

sites.name: Coppermine Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: This shelter accomdates approximately 6 people. However, there is no privy or designated tentsites. Please practice low impact camping practices.

sites.name: Eliza Brook Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Eliza Brook Shelter and 4 hardened tent pads are located near Eliza Brook off Kinsman Ridge Trail (Appalachian Trail) 2.5 miles south of the South Kinsman summit on the mountain's southern ridge. A composting privy, bear box, and dishwashing area are provided. The site is visited by a roving caretaker.

sites.name: Ethan Pond Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​The Ethan Pond Shelter is located at the eastern shore of the scenic Ethan Pond at the edge of the Pemigewasset Wilderness. sites.name: Franconia Brook Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Franconia Brook Tentsite is located on the Eastside trail, on the East side of the Pemigewasset River, 3 miles in from the Lincoln Woods trailhead. There are approximately 20 tentsites available for overnight use. The tentsites are first come, first served, include a fire ring and are designated by a numbered stake…

sites.name: Garfield Ridge Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​The Garfield Ridge Shelter is located at approximately 3,900 ft. on the eastern shoulder of Mt. Garfield just off the Garfield Ridge Trail (Appalachain Trail). sites.name: Guyot Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: This shelter and accompanying tentsites is located on a spur path at 4,360 ft. off the Bondcliff Trail between Mt. Guyot (pronounced Gee-O) and Mt. sites.name: Hexacuba Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Built and maintained by the Dartmouth Outing Club, this 8-person hexagonal shelter is located on a 0.2 mile spur path off Kodiak Trail (Appalachian Trail) 1.6 miles south of the south peak of Mt. sites.name: Jeffers Brook Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Jeffers Brook Shelter is an 'Adirondack' style shelter that is located just off Town Line Trail (Appalachain Trail) via a side trail 1.1 miles north of NH RT 25 in the village of Glencliff. sites.name: Kinsman Pond Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Kinsman Pond Shelter lies on the northern shore of Kinsman Pond at the elevation of 3,750 ft. at the junctions of Kinsman Pond, Kinsman Ridge, and Fishin' Jiminy(AppalachianTrai)Trails. The shelter handles 12 people and there are 1 group and 3 single tent platforms. There is a composting outhouse, dishwashing area…

sites.name: Liberty Springs Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​This tentside, built and maintained by the Appalachain Mountain Club, is situated on Mt. Liberty off the Liberty Spring Trail (Appalachian Trail) 0.3 miles below the junction with the Franconia Ridge Trail. There are seven single and three double tentpads. sites.name: Moose Mountain Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest

sites.name: Smarts Mountain Campsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Originally built by the NH Forest Service, the former Fire Warden's cabin is now maintained by the Dartmouth Outing Club. sites.name: Thirteen Falls Tentsite
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​The remote 13 Falls Tentsite is located near the junction of the Franconia Brook, Lincoln Brook and Twin Brook Trails in the heart of the Pemigewasset Wilderness. There are 9 tent pads available, as well as a bear box, composting privy, and dishwashing area. Seasonal caretaker.

sites.name: Three Ponds Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: Located 2.3 miles from the Three Ponds trailhead, the Three Ponds shelter is situated steps away from the second of three scenic trailside ponds. The shelter sleeps 8 and features a fire ring. However, there is no toilet and no designated tent sites.

sites.name: Trapper John Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Built and maintained by the Dartmouth Outing Club, the Trapper John Shelter is located 1.1 miles from Dorchester Road via Holts Ledge Trail (Appalachian Trail) and spur trail. The 3-walled shelter can accommodate 8 people. The site has a composting privy and a fire ring. There is a water source nearby.

sites.name: Tripoli Road Camping Area
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​Tripoli Road is a very popular area for those seeking a roadside camping experience. This area is not a good choice for campers seeking a tranquil out of the way spot. It is reached by taking exit 31 off Interstate 93. Travel east on Tripoli Road two miles to the registration trailer.

sites.name: Velvet Rocks Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · White Mountain National Forest
sites.description: ​The Velvet Rocks Shelter is located on the Velvet Rocks Trail 1.2 miles from the official western terminus of the trail near NH Rte 120 and Chase Field House in Hanover. A privy is located nearby. Water is accessed along the loop trail but may be unreliable in dry months.

sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Tongass National Forest
sites.description: Entry and Information site for the Nemo Campsites on Wrangell Island. Information boards provide posted information for the public.

sites.name: North Wrangell High Country Shelter
sites.agency: USDA Forest Service · Tongass National Forest
sites.description: The North Wrangell High Country Shelter on Wrangell Island is a 3-sided shelter accessible by hiking the North Wrangell Trail. Located at the highest point along the trail, the site provides excellent views of the mainland and surrounding islands. .

sites.description: The Thoms Creek Crossing Campsite is a fully accessible, single occupancy campsite on the south end of Wrangell Island. Access is via a short footpath from the parking area at the bridge to the site on the shore of Thom's Creek.
